decision: Compare Japanese long narration against the latest selected output, not just the weaker default.
why: The latest artifact uses index rate 1.0 while generate.py still uses 0.25.

decision: Use pooled ECAPA cosine similarity against two existing reference recordings.
why: Positive control scores 0.6254, different-speaker control 0.0897, source TTS 0.0143, default conversion 0.4360, and latest selected conversion 0.5077.
result: Sensitivity confirmed. This is not a listening score or identity percentage.

decision: Screen eight configurations, then validate finalists on held-out speech and five fixed seeds before full-length validation.
why: Require at least 0.015 absolute cosine gain over index-one baseline, both references improving, and full-script character error rate no more than 0.01 above the selected baseline.
result: Freeze metric and acceptance criteria. Do not claim speed or perceptual improvement.

decision: Reject pitch shifts, reduced retrieval, and disabled consonant protection as improvements.
why: All seven variants score below the fixed-seed index-one baseline on the tuning excerpt.

decision: Compare Keita with AndrewMultilingual and BrianMultilingual on the same Japanese paragraph.
why: Pitch changes did not help. A different source can change delivery without modifying the RVC model.
result: All three source files recognized as Japanese. Conversion comparison pending.

decision: Keep the Japanese default unchanged until the quality gate passes.
why: The selected index-one output has 56 character errors versus 24 for the default output on 847 normalized characters.
result: ASR differences include orthographic variation and are not human listening judgments.

why: On the same Japanese paragraph, pooled cosine scores are 0.55106 for Andrew, 0.51079 for Keita, and 0.49936 for Brian. Both reference recordings favor Andrew.
result: Provisional candidate. Full narration and five-seed checks still required.

decision: Run repeated-seed validation and full narration conversion in separate processes with disjoint outputs.
why: Neither job reports timing. Both reuse the existing manifest runner and preserve previous artifacts.
result: No production edits while validation is pending.

decision: Confirm the Andrew source gain across five seeds on each of two paragraphs.
why: Tuning median rises from 0.51187 to 0.56784. Held-out median rises from 0.53474 to 0.55977. Both reference recordings improve in both groups.
result: Source identity proxy gain reproduced. It does not prove perceptual identity.

decision: Reject Andrew at index rate 1.0 for final delivery.
why: The full recording scores 0.56530 but has 86 of 847 character errors, exceeding the frozen gate. The pre-conversion source has only 24 errors.
result: Test retrieval rates 0.65 and 0.8 without changing the source, seed, pitch, or model.

decision: Select Andrew with retrieval rate 0.8 for the existing long narration.
why: Full-script cosine is 0.54318 versus 0.50769 previously, and both files have 56 of 847 character errors. Rate 0.65 reduces errors to 48 but misses the 0.015 similarity gain gate.
result: Full-artifact gate passes. Final-setting short-prompt generalization check is pending.

decision: Preserve all old audio and publish the selected candidate separately.
why: The delivered WAV is byte-identical to the measured candidate and decodes fully with ffmpeg. The clearer original default still has fewer ASR errors, so its settings stay unchanged.
result: No production code or default profile changed.

decision: Accept the balanced candidate for this narration and keep generation defaults unchanged.
why: At retrieval rate 0.8, five-seed median gains are 0.03925 on the tuning paragraph and 0.01559 on the held-out paragraph. Both reference medians improve. The weaker held-out interview gain and the original default's lower ASR errors argue against a global cutover.
result: All candidate delivery gates pass. Broader generalization and perceptual similarity remain unverified.
